solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pressure inside sets a broken bone

indicators.note: inside tells us the pressure letter is placed within the other letters
broken says the letters of sets and a are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A doctor applies pressure to set a broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns SETS A into STAES; 'inside' puts P within it. 'broken bone' looks like one phrase, but 'broken' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup-shaped stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body.

clue.text: Sweeping by, carrying nothing

indicators.note: carrying means the by word holds the nothing letter

parts.note: by in the sense via or by means of is through
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps past, carrying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping reforms are thorough ones, complete and wide-ranging.

clue.text: Scales maybe overturned, all fruit on top

indicators.note: on top places the fruit above the turned word in this down entry

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum, a fruit

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word all is read upwards

explanation.surface: Kitchen scales have been knocked over, fruit all over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like weighing gear, but it is Prunella Scales, the British actress of Fawlty Towers. 'overturned' gives LLA under PRUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is the first name of the British actress Prunella Scales, so an example of Scales.

clue.text: Least affected after sleep

parts.note: since means after a past time, as in since lunch
rest is sleep or repose

explanation.surface: Someone is least affected after a good sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means put on or feigned, so the least affected is the most genuine.

clue.text: Comic actor faces circling press

indicators.note: circling means the word for faces goes round the word for press

parts.note: the faces of a cube or box are its sides
to press or squeeze is to jam

explanation.surface: A comedian pulls faces while the press gathers round him.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid James was a British comic actor, best known for the Carry On films; 'faces' reads as expressions but means sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Sid James was a much-loved British film and television comedian, star of many Carry On comedies.

clue.text: Bust confined, short crack in girdle

indicators.note: in means the confined and crack letters go inside the girdle word

parts.note: a sash is a band worn round the waist, a girdle
confined means trapped

indicators.note: short means the crack word loses its last letter

parts.note: to crack a lock or safe is to force it

explanation.surface: A bust confined in a girdle has a short crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the E of the crack word; the insertion goes after the girdle's first letter. 'Bust' looks like the chest, but means broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bust is to be broke, with no money at all.

clue.text: Analytical details rubbish and enormous

indicators.note: details means both words lose their tails, their last letters

parts.note: junk is rubbish
giant means enormous

explanation.surface: An analysis condemns the details as rubbish and the whole as huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'details' cuts K from JUNK and T from GIANT. 'Analytical' looks generic, but Carl Jung founded analytical psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung's school is called analytical psychology, so his followers are analytical in that sense.

clue.text: Wind that will cover one's bad hearing

indicators.note: will cover means the wind word goes round the one letter

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wind that drowns out a poor hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad hearing' looks like deafness, but a hearing is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial voided by a procedural error is a court hearing gone wrong.

clue.text: Rich kid soldiers almost boot out

parts.note: a kid is a child, a son
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the boot-out word is dropped

parts.note: to boot out is to oust

explanation.surface: A rich child's bodyguards nearly throw someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich voice is deep and full, the sound described as resonant.

clue.text: Firm has one year to accept spymaster as post

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to accept means the year word takes the spymaster's letter into itself

parts.note: a lunar year, twelve lunar months, is one kind of year
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A company recruits a spy chief for a year to fill a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job, but it is an upright pillar; a lunar year is about 354 days long.
explanation.definitionFit: Columnar means shaped like a column or pillar, which is what an upright post is.

clue.text: Concert will go ahead after run initially cancelled?

indicators.note: after places the go-ahead letters following the shortened run
initially cancelled says the first letter of run is removed

parts.note: an event that will go ahead is still on, so it IS ON

explanation.surface: A concert will go ahead after the run of shows was first called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is the definition through the phrase in concert, meaning together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in concert, together and at the same time.

clue.text: Weed holding mediocre record in hand?

indicators.note: holding means the weeding word wraps round the mediocre word

parts.note: to weed a garden is to hoe it
meh is slang for unimpressive or mediocre
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A gardener weeds while holding a so-so record in one hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A home help is a person paid to help an elderly or ill person with housework, so a hired hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic helper can be called a hand, a worker; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Copy of newspaper

definitions.meaning: to copy someone is to imitate their actions exactly
the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a copy of the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: imitating as a reflection does, and the title of a British tabloid.

clue.text: Falsify info about the writer's subjects

parts.note: to falsify is to lie

indicators.note: about means the info word goes round the writer's word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
the writer refers to the setter, giving ME

explanation.surface: Someone falsifies information about the author's subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subjects' looks like topics, but it means people owing loyalty to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a vassal sworn to serve a feudal lord, a subject in that sense.

clue.text: Driven away or drowned in cut

indicators.note: drowned in means or is submerged within the cut word

parts.note: excised means cut out

explanation.surface: A spirit is banished or drowned in a cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorcised describes evil spirits that have been cast out or expelled.

clue.text: Stop suffering, you might say

indicators.note: you might say means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: woe is grief or suffering

explanation.surface: A plea to end the suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you might say' tells you WOE is only heard, and the answer is its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The call riders use to halt a horse is an order to stop.

clue.text: With doctor absent, I refuse to go in it

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means tamper with, so absent and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: With the doctor away, a patient declines to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a GP, but it is the verb to tamper, shuffling ABSENT I. 'refuse' looks like a verb, but it is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for rubbish is where refuse is put.

clue.text: Small cog integral to very big ideas

indicators.note: integral to means the cog word sits within the very big letters

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing label for very large
a pinion is a small cogwheel

explanation.surface: A small cog is integral to some very big ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views or beliefs, ideas someone holds.

clue.text: Some enormous plateau around mountains

indicators.note: around tells us the concealed letters run backwards
some says only part of the words enormous plateau is wanted

explanation.surface: Part of a huge plateau is ringed by mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SPLA from enormouS PLAteau; 'around' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: 'Thing' minus 100 as an arithmetical process

indicators.note: minus says the hundred letter is taken away

parts.note: having a thing about something is an obsession or addiction
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Taking a hundred from something is described as a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minus' looks like part of the arithmetic, but it is the removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding numbers together is one of the four basic operations of arithmetic.

clue.text: Way old man's passionate when he's rejected

parts.note: pa is father, an old man

indicators.note: rejected means the he letters are thrown out of the passionate word

parts.note: vehement means forceful and passionate
he's gives the letters HE, the word he

explanation.surface: Father turns passionate when he is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' looks like a reversal, but it removes HE from VEHEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the pavement is the footway beside a road, a way for walkers.

clue.text: Good man to furnish town

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
to furnish someone with something is to afford it to them

explanation.surface: A kind man pays to furnish a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Without French club, no new stadium in Milan

parts.note: sans is French for without

indicators.note: no says the new letter is left out

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A French club without a new stadium in Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: San Siro is the football ground shared by AC Milan and Inter Milan.

clue.text: Occupier, one in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: in means the one word sits inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: An occupier is described as a person living in a temporary home.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a renter who occupies property owned by someone else.

clue.text: Fence, wide one perhaps

definitions.meaning: a fence is someone who handles stolen goods
a wide ... is a catching position in American football

explanation.surface: A broad fence, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' suggests a garden barrier, but here it is a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A handler of stolen property and a pass-catching player in American football share this name.

clue.text: Rapper's partner that is after good dance

indicators.note: after places the that-is letters behind the good letter

parts.note: boo is hip-hop slang for a boyfriend or girlfriend
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A rapper's partner says this is good dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Boogie is lively dancing to rock or pop music, or the act of dancing that way.

clue.text: An American without life support?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the American letters surround the life word

parts.note: variety is the spice of life, so spice stands for zest or life

explanation.surface: An American is left with no life support machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 'life support' looks like one phrase but splits; life is spice as in variety is the spice of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their patronage or backing.

clue.text: Pretty good UN school, free

indicators.note: free says the letters of UN school are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent United Nations school that charges no fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no-cost education, but it signals the rearrangement of UNSCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no slouch is an idiom praising them as rather capable.

clue.text: Fork out on engagement rings

indicators.note: rings means the engagement word surrounds on

parts.note: a date is an appointment or engagement

explanation.surface: Someone pays out for engagement rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement rings' looks like jewellery, but 'rings' is a verb meaning surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To fork out money is to give it, and to donate is to give it freely.
